narr: A slowly lifting warm front across Arkansas led to a significant rain event across central and northern Arkansas during a period of several days. Rainfall totals mounted across the northern half of the state and by January 30th locations across central and northern Arkansas experienced Flash Flooding after receiving additional rainfall.
ev: The US-Highway 270 bridge over the Ouachita River just east of Pencil Bluff was closed due to high water.
Reported via mPING of multiple basements flooded and creeks overflowing their banks east of the center of Vilonia.
Flooding covered Arkansas Highway 307 making it impassable along with several other roads within Yell County.
Portions of Arkansas Highway 80 were closed due to water over the roadway.
High water from Myers Creek was observed via a social media post flowing across Caddo Gap Road making it impassable.
Arkansas Highway 224 was closed in both directions due to high water from Cattail Creek over the roadway near the community of Swifton.

COOP observer reported that 4.3 inches of total rainfall had fallen over the course of the heavy rain event with high water over multiple local roads and low water bridges in and around the community of Damascus.
Arkansas Highway 175 was closed in both directions due to high water just north of Lake Cherokee on the northern side of Cherokee Village.
Report via social media displayed several roads within the vicinity of Augsburg that were covered by high water.
The intersection of Arkansas Highway 115 and Arkansas Highway 117 was closed due to high water.
Arkansas Highway 80 was closed in both directions due to high water over the highway.
